title: Advanced coaching: concurrent-training interference, goal priority conflicts, periodisation (deload, taper, hypertrophy and marathon blocks)
steps:
PERIODISATION & INTERFERENCE ENGINE (PRD §2, §5; milestones M7). Extend the deterministic programming domain (src/lib/domain/programming + services) — rules as data, explainable, unit-tested:
- Whole-schedule load model: per-day and rolling fatigue by system (lower-body strength, upper-body strength, running/aerobic, Muay Thai/combat, CNS/high-intensity) using planned and logged sessions (sRPE, volume, intensity, impact).
- Interference rules (with explanations): no heavy squats/deadlifts the day before hard Muay Thai/sparring; no high-volume legs before a long run; no intense intervals right after a very demanding day; space hard days; place strength before endurance on the same day when needed, with sufficient separation; respect goal priority when conflicts can't be avoided and EXPLAIN the tradeoff. A validator that scores a week and lists violations, and a scheduler that repairs/minimises them.
- Goal priority conflicts: which goal wins when demands conflict (rank + proximity of event dates), maintenance doses for lower-priority goals (e.g. maintain strength with reduced volume during marathon peak).
- Block types: strength accumulation/intensification/realisation, hypertrophy blocks (weekly sets per muscle within target ranges, progressive volume, rep ranges, RPE), marathon/half-marathon blocks (base → build → peak → taper with progressive mileage ≤ ~10%/week guidance unless justified, long-run progression, race-specific workouts), fight camp for Muay Thai (sparring load, conditioning), deloads (scheduled and reactive: triggered by fatigue/performance decline signals from M6 analytics), tapers before events, maintenance phases.
- Running programming: easy/tempo/intervals/long runs from current fitness (recent race times → training paces via a documented formula), HR zones when available.
- Hook into M6 cycle review and the M3/M6 generators so new cycles use these rules; everything recorded as decisions with rationale.

COACH INTEGRATION & EXPLANATIONS: expose the engine to the M5 agent as tools (evaluate_week_interference, explain_schedule_tradeoffs, plan_block, schedule_deload, plan_taper) returning structured results; proposals created through the M5 lifecycle; the coach explains tradeoffs using engine output (facts/metrics/recommendations labelled). UI: in Train week view, show interference warnings and the 'why' for placements (subtle, premium — not alarm-heavy), a block/periodisation timeline view (phases leading to event dates), deload/taper indicators; Profile goal priority changes trigger a re-plan proposal. axe zero violations both themes; budgets green.

SCENARIO TESTS & JOURNEYS: scenario tests (domain + MockProvider) for every PRD §5 conflict example and §2 multi-goal example: Muay Thai fight + maintain strength + marathon + build muscle; heavy squats vs next-day hard Muay Thai; high-volume legs vs long run; intervals after a demanding day; marathon taper with strength maintenance; hypertrophy block volume progression; reactive deload after declining performance; goal priority swap mid-block. Playwright journey with multiple concurrent disciplines: onboarding with strength + marathon (event date) + Muay Thai Tue/Thu → generated program respects interference rules → week view shows warnings/explanations → change goal priorities → re-plan proposal → accept → new version; screenshots. Update docs (programming rules reference doc with every rule and its rationale, architecture, milestones).
acceptance: A whole-schedule load model and interference validator/scheduler implement the PRD §5 concurrent-training rules as explainable data-driven rules; every placement/conflict decision records a rationale.

Scenario tests (domain + MockProvider) pass for every PRD §5 conflict example and the PRD §2 multi-goal example (fight + strength maintenance + marathon + hypertrophy), including goal-priority tradeoffs with explanations.

Block types are supported and tested: strength phases, hypertrophy (weekly sets per muscle within ranges, progressive volume), marathon/half (base→build→peak→taper with progressive mileage and long-run progression), fight camp, scheduled and reactive deloads (triggered by M6 fatigue/performance signals), tapers before events, maintenance doses.
The coach can evaluate, explain and propose schedule/block changes through new tools using the engine output; proposals go through the confirmation lifecycle.

Playwright: a multiple-concurrent-disciplines journey (strength + marathon + Muay Thai) shows a program that respects interference rules with explanations, and a goal-priority change produces a re-plan proposal that, when accepted, creates a new version.
UI for interference warnings, placement 'why', periodisation timeline and deload/taper indicators is premium and calm; axe zero violations in both themes; budgets and perf guard green.
All gates pass locally; a programming rules reference doc lists every rule with rationale; work committed on feat/m7-advanced-coaching with Conventional Commits.
